HYPOTHESIS (final, public submission, in English):

"The relative advantage in bachelor's (BA) degree completion for Black students is most pronounced at the HIGHEST socioeconomic levels, where the completion-rate gap relative to White students narrows to a minimum and essentially disappears, whereas it is wide and significant at lower SES levels. Specifically, within the top SES quartile Q4 Black students reach 3.03% vs 3.67% for White (−0.64 percentage points; rate ratio 0.83; Fisher exact p=0.72, statistically indistinguishable), compared with Q1 (−1.34 pp, ratio 0.25, p=0.017), Q2 (−2.99 pp, ratio 0.31, p=0.0003) and Q3 (−2.10 pp, ratio 0.44, p=0.025). Consistently, a continuous logistic model (BA ~ SES×race) shows the BA–SES gradient is significantly steeper for Black students (SES_z slope 0.726, OR=2.07) than for White (slope 0.161; interaction p=0.003), so the log-odds gap relative to White narrows from ~1.81 at low SES to ~0.12 at high SES, and the predicted Black/White completion ratio climbs monotonically from 0.17 at SES_z=−1.5 to 0.89 at SES_z=+1.5. Robustness with SES tertiles (ratio 0.14→0.58) and a Black-vs-rest comparison (0.33→0.82) reproduces the same monotonic pattern. Caveat: this is a RELATIVE advantage — the data show no absolute advantage (Black students never exceed White completion rates); the advantage manifests as increasingly close parity with White students as SES rises, with Black students' completion rising far more steeply with SES."

WORKFLOW (executed): (1) loaded data/nls_ses_processed.csv (8,773 rows, 8 cols, no missing); (2) computed per-race and per-SES BA completion rates, SES cut into full-sample quartiles (primary) and tertiles (robustness); (3) for each SES level, 2×2 Black-vs-White (and Black-vs-rest) tables with percentage-point difference, rate ratio and Fisher exact test; (4) continuous logistic regression BA ~ SES_z*RACE to test whether the SES gradient differs by race and to quantify the narrowing log-odds gap; (5) consolidated traceable evidence written to analysis/evidence_summary.txt. All scripts executed with non-empty output.
